questions.stem: Under the Code on CIS, the trustee of a retail scheme is primarily responsible for:

options.A: Making investment decisions for the scheme
options.B: Marketing and distributing the scheme to retail investors
options.C: Preparing the prospectus for MAS registration
options.D: Safeguarding the assets of the scheme and ensuring the manager complies with the trust deed

questions.explanation: The trustee's role under the Code on CIS is to hold and safeguard scheme assets, act in unitholders' interests, and ensure the scheme manager complies with the trust deed and regulations. Investment decisions are made by the manager. Marketing and distribution are the manager's and distributor's functions. Prospectus preparation is the manager's responsibility.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06 on AML/CFT, a financial adviser is required to terminate a business relationship in which of the following circumstances?

options.A: The client's income increases significantly, triggering a new risk tier
options.B: The client requests a transfer to a competitor FA firm
options.C: The FA is unable to complete CDD due to the client's refusal to provide required information
options.D: The client has not transacted for more than 12 months

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 requires a financial adviser to terminate (or not establish) a business relationship when the FA is unable to complete the required CDD because the client refuses to provide necessary information. In such cases, the FA should also consider filing an STR. Increased client income, transfers, and inactivity are not grounds for mandatory termination.

questions.stem: Under the Ethics framework, 'moral courage' in the context of a financial adviser means:

options.A: Willingness to challenge the firm's management when ethical standards are being compromised
options.B: Willingness to recommend high-risk products to maximise client returns
options.C: Ability to make quick decisions under time pressure during client meetings
options.D: Confidence in promoting one's own services over competitors

questions.explanation: Moral courage in professional ethics means having the willingness to speak up, challenge, or act when ethical standards are being violated - even when it is personally costly to do so, such as challenging management decisions or reporting misconduct. It is not about risk appetite, decisiveness under pressure, or competitive self-promotion.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the 'suitability' obligation of a financial adviser under the FAA?

options.A: The adviser must recommend only the cheapest product available for each need
options.B: The adviser must recommend only products from the firm's approved product list regardless of the client's needs
options.C: The adviser must recommend products approved by both MAS and the client's employer
options.D: The adviser must have a reasonable basis that the recommendation is appropriate for the client's specific circumstances

questions.explanation: The suitability obligation requires the adviser to have a reasonable basis - grounded in knowing the client's circumstances, needs, risk profile, and objectives - that the recommendation is appropriate for that specific client. It does not mandate the cheapest product, dual approvals, or rigid adherence to an approved list if the product does not suit the client.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, which of the following is NOT one of the key elements of Customer Due Diligence (CDD)?

options.A: Identifying the customer and verifying the customer's identity
options.B: Identifying the beneficial owner and verifying the beneficial owner's identity
options.C: Conducting a credit assessment to determine the client's ability to invest
options.D: Understanding the nature and purpose of the business relationship

questions.explanation: CDD under FAA-N06 comprises: (i) identifying and verifying the customer, (ii) identifying and verifying the beneficial owner, (iii) understanding the nature and purpose of the business relationship, and (iv) ongoing monitoring. A credit assessment is a suitability and lending tool, not a CDD requirement under AML/CFT rules.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, 'ongoing monitoring' of a business relationship requires which of the following?

options.A: Scrutinising transactions to ensure they are consistent with the FA's knowledge of the client and their source of funds
options.B: Contacting the client once per year by telephone to confirm personal details
options.C: Filing an STR for every transaction above S$5,000
options.D: Reviewing the client's investment portfolio performance quarterly

questions.explanation: Ongoing monitoring under FAA-N06 involves scrutinising transactions conducted throughout the relationship to ensure they are consistent with the FA's understanding of the client, their business, and their source of funds - and to identify any unusual or suspicious activity. Annual telephone calls, STRs for every S$5,000 transaction, and portfolio performance reviews are not the prescribed ongoing monitoring activities.

questions.stem: A representative fails to submit a required MAS regulatory return on time. This is an example of which category of ethical failure?

options.A: Misrepresentation
options.B: Churning
options.C: Negligence or failure to comply with regulatory obligations

questions.explanation: Failing to comply with a regulatory obligation (such as timely submission of required returns) is a failure of professional responsibility and regulatory compliance - classified as negligence or non-compliance. It is distinct from misrepresentation (making false statements), churning (excessive switching), or conflict of interest (personal interest affecting recommendations).

questions.stem: Under the FAA, a licensed financial adviser that conducts regulated activity while its licence is suspended commits an offence. The maximum fine is:
questions.explanation: Conducting regulated activity while a financial adviser's licence is suspended is a serious offence under the FAA, attracting a maximum fine of S$150,000. This is significantly higher than other FAA fines because it involves deliberate operation outside authorised status. S$50,000 is the cap for offences such as permitting unqualified reps. S$25,000 applies to the acting-for-multiple-principals offence.

questions.stem: A licensed financial adviser wishes to hold client assets (e.g. securities and cash) directly. Under the FAA and related regulations, the FA must:

options.A: Obtain separate CMS licence for custodial services
options.B: Segregate client assets from the FA's own assets at all times
options.C: File a client asset notification with MAS monthly
options.D: Obtain written consent from each client before holding their assets

questions.explanation: A licensed FA that holds client assets is required to segregate them from its own assets at all times, to protect clients in the event of the FA's insolvency. Holding client assets does not automatically require a CMS licence if it is incidental to the advisory service. There is no monthly MAS notification or general written consent requirement specifically for asset holding in this context.

questions.stem: Under the concept of fair dealing, 'information asymmetry' between a financial adviser and a client is ethically significant because:

options.A: It allows the FA to charge premium fees that other advisers cannot justify
options.B: It requires the FA to apply a fixed fee structure rather than commission
options.C: It means the FA must seek MAS approval before recommending complex products
options.D: It creates a duty on the FA to share relevant information that the client needs to make informed decisions

questions.explanation: Information asymmetry - where the adviser knows significantly more than the client - creates a fiduciary-like duty to share material information. The ethically correct response is to use that knowledge to serve the client, not to exploit the gap. Information asymmetry does not entitle the FA to premium fees, require MAS pre-approval, or mandate a particular fee structure.

questions.stem: Under the FAA and AML/CFT rules, a 'beneficial owner' is BEST described as:

options.A: The individual whose name appears on the investment account
options.B: The legal trustee acting on behalf of a trust
options.C: The nominee shareholder of the customer company
options.D: The natural person who ultimately owns or controls the customer

questions.explanation: A beneficial owner under FAA-N06 and AML/CFT frameworks is the natural person who ultimately owns or exercises control over the customer, behind any legal or nominee structures. The account holder may be a company or nominee. The nominee shareholder and legal trustee are intermediary structures - the beneficial owner is the ultimate natural person behind them.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, which of the following statements about reliance on third-party CDD is correct?

options.A: If CDD is conducted by a third party, the financial adviser bears no further responsibility for the adequacy of that CDD
options.B: The FA may rely on CDD conducted by a group entity that is subject to equivalent AML/CFT supervision
options.C: Third-party CDD reliance is only permitted for institutional clients, never for individuals
options.D: The FA must obtain MAS written approval before relying on any third-party CDD

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 permits reliance on third-party CDD conducted by group entities subject to equivalent AML/CFT supervision, subject to conditions. However, the FA always remains ultimately responsible for the adequacy of CDD - responsibility cannot be fully delegated. Third-party reliance is not limited to institutional clients. MAS written approval is not required for each instance of third-party reliance.

questions.stem: The CPF MediSave contribution requirement for self-employed persons applies when their annual net trade income exceeds:
questions.explanation: Self-employed persons in Singapore must contribute to MediSave if their annual net trade income exceeds S$6,000. The contribution rate ranges from 4% to 10.5% depending on age. S$2,000 and S$4,000 are below the threshold. S$10,000 is not the prescribed threshold.

questions.stem: A representative discovers that a competitor has been making misleading comparative statements about her firm's products in client meetings. Under the ethics framework, the BEST initial response is:

options.A: Raise the matter with her firm's compliance or management so the issue can be addressed through proper channels
options.B: Make equally aggressive counter-claims about the competitor's products in client meetings
options.C: File an STR with STRO as the competitor's conduct may involve fraud
options.D: Contact the competitor's clients directly to correct the misinformation

questions.explanation: The appropriate response to a competitor's misconduct is to raise it through the firm's internal compliance or management channels, who can escalate through regulatory or industry channels if warranted. Retaliating with counter-claims perpetuates misinformation. Filing an STR is for money laundering/terrorism, not competitor marketing misconduct. Contacting the competitor's clients is inappropriate and potentially in breach of data privacy rules.

questions.stem: Under MAS Guidelines G04 on Risk Management of Internet Banking Services, financial institutions must implement controls to protect against unauthorized access. Which of the following is NOT one of the prescribed controls?

options.A: Multi-factor authentication for online transactions
options.B: Automatic session timeout after a period of inactivity
options.C: Real-time monitoring of all client transactions for pattern anomalies
options.D: Requiring clients to use only MAS-approved internet browsers

questions.explanation: MAS G04 requires multi-factor authentication, session timeout, and transaction monitoring as controls for internet banking. However, restricting clients to MAS-approved browsers is not a prescribed control under G04 - this would be technically impractical and is not an approach taken in the guidelines.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required in all of the following situations EXCEPT:

options.A: When the customer is a PEP
options.B: When the customer is a Singaporean citizen with verified employment
options.C: When the transaction involves a country with known AML/CFT deficiencies
options.D: When the business relationship is conducted on a non-face-to-face basis

questions.explanation: EDD is required for PEPs, high-risk countries, and non-face-to-face relationships (among other high-risk factors) under FAA-N06. A Singaporean citizen with verified employment and no other risk factors is a standard-risk customer who requires ordinary CDD, not enhanced due diligence. Citizenship alone is not an EDD trigger.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes the concept of 'tipping off' under AML/CFT rules?

options.A: Providing unsolicited financial advice to a client without a prior engagement
options.B: Informing a client or third party that an STR has been filed or is being contemplated
options.C: Revealing a competitor's business strategies to clients
options.D: Disclosing a product's risk factors before the client asks

questions.explanation: Tipping off is the criminal act of informing a person who is the subject of an STR (or potential STR) that a report has been filed or is being contemplated, which could allow them to take steps to avoid detection. Unsolicited advice, revealing competitor information, and proactive risk disclosure are unrelated to tipping off.

questions.stem: Under the Code on CIS, a collective investment scheme that invests at least 70% of its net asset value in real estate-related assets and is listed on the Singapore Exchange is known as:

options.A: A hedge fund
options.B: A business trust

questions.explanation: A listed CIS that invests at least 70% of its NAV in real estate assets and real estate-related investments is a REIT under the Code on CIS. Hedge funds are typically exempt from the Code. Business trusts operate differently under the Business Trusts Act. SPACs are acquisition vehicles, not income-generating real estate funds.

questions.stem: A client, Lim Beng Hock, aged 50, asks for a product to provide monthly income in retirement at age 65. He has low risk tolerance. Which of the following approaches is MOST consistent with suitability requirements?

options.A: Recommend a 100% equity unit trust because it provides the highest long-term return
options.B: Advise him to leave all savings in the OA to benefit from the 2.5% guarantee
options.C: Recommend a geared property investment fund to maximize income potential
options.D: Recommend an annuity or a capital-guaranteed retirement income plan aligned with his low risk tolerance and income objective

questions.explanation: For a client with low risk tolerance seeking retirement income, suitability requires recommending capital-protected or income-generating products such as annuities or guaranteed retirement income plans. Equity-heavy, geared, or property investments are inconsistent with low risk tolerance. While OA savings are safe, leaving all assets there ignores inflation risk and the income objective.

questions.stem: Under the framework for ethical behaviour, which of the following MOST accurately describes the difference between a 'rule-based' and 'principle-based' approach to ethics?

options.A: Rule-based ethics focuses on compliance with specific prescribed rules; principle-based ethics focuses on acting according to broader values even when no specific rule applies
options.B: Rule-based ethics requires advisers to follow MAS rules; principle-based ethics is optional
options.C: Principle-based ethics permits advisers to breach rules if the broader principle is satisfied
options.D: Rule-based ethics applies only to products; principle-based ethics applies only to client relationships

questions.explanation: Rule-based ethics involves complying with specific prescriptive rules; principle-based ethics guides conduct through broader values (such as fairness, honesty, and acting in the client's best interest) in situations where no specific rule applies. Principle-based ethics complements rules but does not permit rule breaches. Both apply across all areas of the business.

questions.stem: MAS Notice FAA-N06 requires financial advisers to adopt a risk-based approach to AML/CFT. What does this mean in practice?

options.A: Applying the same level of CDD to every customer regardless of risk factors
options.B: Filing STRs for all customers classified as medium or high risk
options.C: Allocating more resources and scrutiny to higher-risk customers and relationships
options.D: Refusing to serve customers from high-risk jurisdictions

questions.explanation: A risk-based approach means calibrating the intensity of CDD and ongoing monitoring to the assessed risk level of each customer relationship. Higher-risk relationships receive more intensive scrutiny. Universal application of the same level to all customers is inefficient and not a risk-based approach. STR obligations are triggered by suspicion, not risk classification alone. Refusing all high-risk-country clients is disproportionate and not required.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about the CPF Retirement Account (RA)?

options.A: The RA is opened when a member turns 55 and is credited with savings from the OA and SA
options.B: The RA is opened for all CPF members from birth
options.C: The RA pays 2.5% interest guaranteed per annum
options.D: The RA may be used to pay HDB housing loan installments

questions.explanation: The CPF Retirement Account is created when a member turns 55. Savings from the OA and SA are transferred to the RA (up to the applicable retirement sum) at that time. The RA earns a minimum of 4% p.a. (not 2.5%, which is the OA rate). RA savings are designated for retirement income and cannot be used for HDB housing loans.

questions.stem: A client, Tan Siew Eng, aged 55, has the following CPF balances: OA = S$150,000, SA = S$120,000, MA = S$60,000. The Full Retirement Sum (FRS) at her 55th birthday is S$205,000. How much will remain in her OA after the RA is created?
questions.explanation: RA creation draws first from SA, then from OA if needed. SA = S$120,000 which is less than FRS of S$205,000. Shortfall = S$205,000 - S$120,000 = S$85,000 drawn from OA. OA remainder = S$150,000 - S$85,000 = S$65,000. SA is reduced to zero (all transferred). MA = S$60,000 is untouched. So OA balance = S$65,000.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice 307, an insurer issuing an ILP must ensure that policy illustrations use a projected investment return of no higher than:

options.A: 4% per annum low scenario and 7% per annum high scenario
options.B: 3% per annum low scenario and 5% per annum high scenario
options.C: 5% per annum low scenario and 9% per annum high scenario
options.D: Any rate the insurer considers realistic based on past performance

questions.explanation: Notice 307 prescribes standardised projection rates for ILP policy illustrations: 4% per annum for the low scenario and 7% per annum for the high scenario. These rates are set by MAS to ensure comparability across products and to avoid misleading projections. Insurers may not use self-selected rates.

questions.stem: Under MAS Notice FAA-N06, a financial adviser must identify the beneficial owner of a legal arrangement (such as a trust). In which case must the FA identify the beneficiaries of the trust?

options.A: When the beneficiaries are named or identified, even if not yet holding any interest
options.B: Always, as all trust beneficiaries are treated as beneficial owners
options.C: Only when the trust has assets above S$1 million
options.D: Only when the trust makes a distribution to a beneficiary

questions.explanation: FAA-N06 requires identification of trust beneficiaries when they are named or sufficiently identified, because these individuals may be the ultimate beneficial owners. It is not limited to high-asset trusts, distributions, or post-distribution events. In class-of-beneficiary situations (where individuals are not yet identified), different rules apply.

questions.stem: A financial adviser firm's compliance officer discovers that three representatives have been signing client fact-find forms on behalf of clients without the clients' knowledge. Under the FAA and ethics framework, the compliance officer should FIRST:

options.A: Escalate the matter internally to senior management and the board, and consider whether a MAS notification is required
options.B: Report the matter immediately to MAS before any internal investigation
options.C: Issue the three representatives a written warning and require them to conduct additional CPD training
options.D: Immediately terminate the three representatives without further action

questions.explanation: The correct response is to escalate the matter to senior management and the board as a matter of urgency, and determine whether notification to MAS is required under the FAA's mandatory reporting obligations. Reporting directly to MAS before any internal investigation may not be appropriate as the first step; the firm must assess the situation. A written warning and CPD training are insufficient responses to a potential forgery issue. Immediate termination without following fair procedure may expose the firm to employment law liability.

questions.stem: Under the CPF framework, which of the following statements about Medisave is correct?

options.A: MediSave can be used to pay for any outpatient medical expenses without restriction
options.B: MediSave contributions are voluntary for employees above age 65
options.C: MediSave may be used to pay premiums for approved insurance schemes such as MediShield Life
options.D: MediSave funds earn a minimum interest of 2.5% per annum

questions.explanation: MediSave may be used to pay premiums for approved schemes such as MediShield Life, CareShield Life, and Integrated Shield Plans. MediSave for outpatient expenses is subject to withdrawal limits (not unlimited). CPF contributions including MediSave remain mandatory for employees below 65 (though reduced rates apply). MA earns a minimum of 4% p.a. (not 2.5%, which is the OA floor).

questions.stem: Under the FAA, a financial adviser is permitted to advertise its services. Which of the following is NOT permitted in an advertisement?

options.A: Stating the firm's MAS licence number
options.B: Providing contact details for the FA's representatives
options.C: Listing the range of financial products the FA is authorised to advise on
options.D: Including testimonials from past clients, without any disclaimer

questions.explanation: Under FAA conduct requirements and MAS guidelines on advertising, client testimonials must not create a misleading impression about the likely performance or outcomes of financial products or services. Using testimonials without appropriate disclaimers (e.g., that past experience is not indicative of future results) violates advertising standards. Stating the licence number, product scope, and contact details are all permissible.

questions.stem: A financial advisory firm is designing its compliance programme. Under the principles of sound compliance management, which of the following is the MOST important characteristic of an effective compliance function?

options.A: The compliance team must be the largest department in the firm by headcount
options.B: The compliance function must conduct at least 50 client audits per year
options.C: The compliance officer must hold a legal degree from a recognised university
options.D: The compliance function must be independent of business line management and have direct reporting access to the board or its audit committee

questions.explanation: An effective compliance function must be independent of the business lines it oversees and have direct access to the board or audit committee so it can escalate concerns without business pressure. Headcount size, academic qualifications of the compliance officer, and a specific number of client audits per year are not prerequisites for an effective compliance function. Independence and board access are the defining characteristics.
